newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Higher Shell profits thanks to Q4.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Higher Shell profits thanks to Q4.

text.p: Higher oil prices, rising production and significantly better chemicals results will have boosted Royal Dutch/Shell Group's fourth quarter performance, boosting the 1996 outcome, analysts said on Friday.
Full-year and fourth quarter results from the group are due on February 13.

Analysts' estimates for 1996 net profit on a current cost basis vary between 5.15 and 5.50 billion stg compared with 4.52 billion in 1995. The forecasts are before exceptional items and are excluding windfall profits or losses resulting from changes in oil prices on stocks.
The dividend for the year is predicted to rise to between 35.0 and 43.0 pence per share from 33.3 pence.
Low inventories and cold weather kept fourth-quarter oil prices at an average $24 per barrel, which was more than $2.50 above the third quarter level and $6.50 higher year-on-year.
Chemical results are expected to have improved sharply compared with 1995's fourth quarter, when prices slumped from their summer peaks, analysts said.

They forecast slightly higher refining margins as markets improved in Rotterdam and Singapore, but the outlook for the refining industry as a whole will remain shaky amid persistent overcapacity and fierce competition.

To fight the poor trading conditions, Shell, Texaco Inc and Star Enterprises, a Texaco joint venture, announced plans to combine their U.S. downstream operations, and analysts hope to hear more about this on Thursday.
Shell said late last month it was near agreement on signing a letter of intent with its partners. The combined downstream operations would control about 11 to 15 percent of the U.S. petroleum market.
The merger plan follows an earlier link-up by Mobil and British Petroleum Co Plc of their European downstream businesses.
Many analysts believe Anglo-Dutch Shell is lagging behind its major rivals in cutting costs and streamlining operations.
"They are slow in restructuring their operations," said Irene Himona at SocGen.
Analysts also want Shell to identify more investment projects to make its huge cash pile work. Shell said last month it had about five to six billion stg free to spend.
